title: Exploring LGBTQ+ Bias in Generative AI Answers across Different Country and Religious Contexts
findings: When prompts included religious context (Orthodox Christian or Conservative Muslim), both ChatGPT 3.5 and Bard significantly reduced their support for LGBTQ+ people. ChatGPT's responses demonstrated a strong tendency towards normative cultural relativism, acknowledging and respecting diverse religious viewpoints. In contrast, Bard, while still adjusting its responses, more frequently maintained a human rights-based framework. The decrease in support for LGBTQ+ issues was more pronounced in religious contexts than in country-specific contexts, particularly for Bard. ChatGPT also reduced its use of content violation warnings when religious contexts were provided.

measurement_description: The study measured how providing the context of a prompter's religious affiliation (Orthodox Christian, Conservative Muslim) influences generative AI responses to homophobic statements. It assessed whether the AI systems' answers align more with a culturally relativistic framework (respecting religious views on homosexuality) or a universal human rights framework (supporting LGBTQ+ rights regardless of context).
